question: When does MSC 6.00AX /Og keep a local array element in a CSE temporary across a call? If the array's address never escapes, a repeated element value (lines[i] passed to two calls) is loaded once into a 4-byte value temporary and pushed from it after the call. Once the array's address has been taken anywhere in the function (p = lines; *p = buf; even when the pointer is otherwise dead and copy-propagated away), the element is assumed to be changed by calls: MSC keeps only the element ADDRESS (lea/add into a 2-byte temporary) and reloads the value after each call; a first-loop 'arr[0][i]' access likewise becomes a spilled far-pointer CSE of arr[0]+i. Positive control root:1629 MakeBalloon (worker resE): exact only with 'lp = lines; *lp = buf;' (frame 110, address temporaries at [bp-0x58], [bp-0x56]); without the address escape the loops keep value temporaries and the function is 1095-1102 bytes instead of 1111.

expect.no_escape@0: mov word ptr [bp - 0x2c], ax; mov word ptr [bp - 0x2a], dx; push dx; push ax
expect.escaped@0: mov word ptr [bp - 0x2a], bx; push word ptr [bx + 2]; push word ptr [bx]
